options.text: does not take into account irrational behaviour.
enables accurate forecasts to be made.
includes a value judgement.
may be true or false.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a nudge technique that could be used to encourage healthy eating?

options.text: Banning supermarkets from selling high-calorie energy drinks
Increasing taxes on high-fat products to raise their price
Moving products with a high sugar content away from supermarket checkouts
Subsidising fruit and vegetables to reduce their prices

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a reason why the extension of property rights is likely to reduce market failure?

options.text: Merit goods will no longer be underconsumed in a free market.
Producers will be more likely to have to pay compensation for pollution.
Public goods will no longer be subject to the free-rider problem.
The inequality in the distribution of income and wealth will be reduced.

options.text: Car manufacturers’ stocks of unsold cars are low
The demand for cars is also price elastic
The marginal cost of producing cars increases significantly with output
There is considerable spare capacity in the car industry

questions.questionText: Changing patterns of consumption have meant that summer holidays at UK seaside towns have become less popular. As a result, UK seaside holiday towns are affected by seasonal unemployment and increasing structural unemployment. Which one of the following is the most likely consequence of this change in the pattern of consumption?

options.text: Occupational immobility of labour will help to reduce structural unemployment.
The cost of living for people who live in UK seaside towns will fall.
Unemployment is likely to be higher in the summer than the winter.
Wages in UK seaside towns will rise because firms want to retain workers.

The total amount paid in wages will increase from (W3 × Q1) to (W1 × Q1).
The wage rate will fall from W1 to W2.
